plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE with outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000 x 11 raw Salmon gene-level counts (human muscle, 5 treated vs 5 control, unpaired, single batch). The PCA/sample-distance profile flags sample_03 as an outlier. Per the grounded knowledge-service procedure for a 5-vs-5 unpaired single-batch design with an outlier flag: (1) run sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA on top-500-variance genes, sample distance heatmap, library-size/detected-gene diagnostics) to characterize sample_03 and look for a technical cause rather than removing it silently; (2) fit DESeq2 twice on the same pre-filtered, median-of-ratios-normalized count matrix — once with all 10 samples (primary, since the smallest group has 5 replicates, above the 3-replicate threshold where the grounded rule prefers down-weighting an outlier over removal) and once with sample_03 excluded (stated-criterion sensitivity run) — each with a Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05; (3) compare the two gene lists explicitly (intersection, genes gained/lost) as the deliverable robustness check; (4) run fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) with Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, on the primary (all-sample) DE result, since >=50 tested genes eliminates the low-N ORA concern; (5) compile a report with fit diagnostics, effect columns, reproducibility record, and the outlier-removal sensitivity comparison as its centerpiece, per the R-0090 flag. All reference gene sets (MSigDB Hallmark human, Reactome, WikiPathways human) are confirmed present in the reference store for this organism.
